headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Roo Code can read/write and use MCP/browser/network, while Airbyte can exfiltrate business data via broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers, so it may ingest Airbyte-produced artifacts or web content as instructions. Airbyte itself only exposes an API and broad egress, so the interaction is indirect rather than a built-in shared channel. The pathway exists in default workspace-based use, but no direct parser hijack is documented.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are saved into the shared VS Code workspace and Roo Code reads them as task context
IF Roo Code ingests browser or MCP content without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in a separate directory not mounted into Roo Code's workspace
Disable or restrict MCP servers for the Roo Code session
Require manual review of any Airbyte-generated text before Roo Code acts on it
Use a read-only export folder for Airbyte artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Airbyte outputs and Roo Code inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Roo Code can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs and MCP servers. If Airbyte outputs land in the shared workspace, Roo Code may transmit them onward. This is a default workspace-flow risk, but not a guaranteed leak because the exact data path is user-configured.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is written into the VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send that workspace context to a third-party model API or MCP server
mitigations: Store Airbyte outputs outside the Roo Code workspace
Limit Roo Code context to non-sensitive files
Disable automatic file attachment for sensitive folders
Review model-provider and MCP destinations before running the pair
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while Airbyte can emit data through APIs and broad egress. If both operate on the same workspace or repo, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or create conflicting state. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, but not unrestricted shared writes to the same directory, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes generated artifacts into the same repository or workspace Roo Code edits
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files while Airbyte is updating the same paths
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches for Roo Code changes and immutable exports for Airbyte
Check in generated files only after manual review
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and browser/MCP outputs, so it may treat Airbyte-produced artifacts as authoritative inputs. Airbyte can generate or move business data, and Roo Code can then transform or operationalize it without a verification step. The pair creates a plausible default cascade, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream actions.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Airbyte-generated files as source-of-truth without validation
IF Roo Code performs follow-on actions based on those files or browser findings
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Roo Code acts on Airbyte outputs
Mark Airbyte exports as untrusted in the workspace
Require schema validation on any Airbyte-produced file
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis for Airbyte artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated checks that compare Airbyte outputs against expected schemas

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is documented as handling business data, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots and can send context to configured model APIs. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow, not either one alone.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte includes regulated records
IF Roo Code is configured to transmit those records to a provider or MCP server with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code prompts and workspace files
Confirm provider retention settings before use
Use separate accounts or tenants for sensitive workflows
Review data-processing terms for any configured model API
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention boundaries
